findings.text: test_scalar_cut_tile_keeps_wide_batches asserts current._SCALAR_CUT_BATCH_WIDTH == 32 while the landed head sets it to 128 at nova/equilibrium/current.py:72, so this test fails deterministically at head; the node's gate ran only tests/test_booking_scalar_tile.py, and a default change to a module must retarget that file's own guard and its lines 35-36 rationale in the same change.

the narrow-tile negative control locates its mutation by the literal '_SCALAR_CUT_BATCH_WIDTH = 32' and asserts source.count(target) == 1; after the landed change the literal is absent, so the control now aborts instead of producing its 16-vs-32 comparison, breaking a prototype control outside this node's scope.

the fragment states 'The fixed scalar cut tile is now _SCALAR_CUT_BATCH_WIDTH = 32' and 'Keeping the scalar width at 32 preserves the measured conic propagation structure'; both sentences are false at head and the record now contradicts the landed default.

the arm change is computed from the first process of each arm only (a[0], b[0]); no verdict flips on the landed numbers, but the arm wall the plan names is the median warm wall, so the adjudication reads one of the two retained processes rather than the median it states.

the inspected artifact is SVG_SHA256=903f9e45 recorded in figure-inspection-final.log, which is the blob at 82bab502d; the committed blob at head is d1d09633, so the provenance record does not name the figure that landed, though the diff between the two is matplotlib element ids and the generator date only.
